findings.title: Loads CA bundle during every import
findings.why_it_matters: Importing requests now synchronously initializes an SSL context and reads the complete default CA bundle, even when the process only makes HTTP requests or never makes a request. Previously, the bundle was supplied when a verified HTTPS connection was configured. This shifts a nonzero startup cost to every process importing Requests, including short-lived workers, while the repeated-load savings only benefit verified TLS traffic.
evidence: Prior revision src/requests/adapters.py:294: cert_loc = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH) (inside cert_verify, reached for HTTPS with verification enabled).
findings.suggested_fix: If startup cost matters for HTTP-only and short-lived processes, initialize and cache the shared context lazily on the first verify=True request, with thread-safe one-time initialization.

residual_risks: The startup cost depends on the platform CA bundle, filesystem, and SSL implementation; this review did not benchmark cold imports against the prior revision.
testing_gaps: No import-time performance measurement was run; the reported cost is the synchronous CA bundle load introduced at module initialization.
